Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Rincewind <snowlock@phantom.com> wrote:
>   Emily is all tapped out because of her earlier actions in a round.  
>Her predator, Mark, now proceeds to bleed her.  However, Ken offers to 
>help Emily (in exchange for later vote support) by untapping one of her 
>minions with Rat's Warning or Wake With Evening's Freshness so that she 
>can block Mark's bleed.  Is that a legal move?...

No.  Action modifiers and reactions only affect the vampire using such
a card unless the card says otherwise.  Both of the cards you mention
specifically say they affect "this vampire", meaning the vampire playing
the card.  See superior Cloak the Gathering for an example of a modifier
which can be used on another minion.

>Another thing the rulebook says is that combat actions go as follows:
>acting minion, blocking minion, other players clockwise.  
>  Does this sequence of play also apply to bleed actions? (i.e., can a 
>reaction card be played out of turn by a methuselah who is not directly 
>affected by the action?)

It is possible for any Methuselah other than the acting player to play
reactions, assuming the reaction card allows it.  The defending player
would get priority in playing reactions; priority for other players reacting
should probably be that of the turn order, starting from the acting player.
